renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: cumulative_coverage_curve
  title: Cumulative coverage
  description: |-
    Each curve is a DNA sample: the fraction of bases covered at least to each depth. It answers how much of the target is sequenced deeply enough to call variants.
    How to read: a curve that stays high and drops late means deep, even coverage. A tumour sequenced deeper than its normal sits to the right. A curve that drops early marks a sample too shallow for the somatic callers you plan to use.
    Lines and annotations: none are drawn. BamTools documents no coverage floor, so judge the depth against the requirements of your callers.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hartwigmedical/hmftools/master/bam-tools/README.md
  kind: profile
  config:
    x_title: Coverage depth (x)
    y_title: Fraction of bases at or above depth
    legend_pos: bottom
  roles:
    series: sample
    x: coverage
    y: fraction_at_least

- component: figure
  title: Coverage depth distribution
  description: |-
    Each line is a sample: the fraction of bases at each exact depth, the density behind the cumulative curve. It answers where the bulk of the coverage sits.
    How to read: a single narrow peak is even coverage. A wide or multi-peaked line means uneven sequencing, and a spike at depth zero is unsequenced bases.
  visu_type: line
  dict_kwargs:
    x: coverage
    y: fraction
    color: sample
    labels:
      coverage: Coverage depth (x)
      fraction: Fraction of bases at this depth
      sample: Sample

- component: table
  title: Coverage table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample and a depth with the bases at that depth, their fraction and the cumulative fraction. It answers the exact numbers behind the curves.
    How to read: filter by sample and read the cumulative fraction at the depth your caller needs.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: fragment_length_curve
  title: Fragment length distribution
  description: |-
    Each curve is a DNA sample: the share of read pairs at each insert size, grouped into equal windows so libraries of different depth overlay. It answers whether the libraries have the expected insert size.
    How to read: one smooth peak is a normal library, and samples of the same prep should overlay. A shifted or bimodal curve points at a library preparation problem.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hartwigmedical/hmftools/master/bam-tools/README.md
  kind: profile
  config:
    x_title: Fragment length (bp)
    y_title: Share of read pairs
    legend_pos: bottom
  roles:
    series: sample
    x: fragment_length
    y: fraction

- component: table
  title: Fragment length table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample and a fragment length window with the read pairs in it and their share. It answers the exact numbers behind the curve.
    How to read: sort by share to find the modal fragment length of each sample.

- component: card
  id: mean_coverage_spread
  title: Mean coverage
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median mean depth over the DNA samples and the box shows the spread. It answers how deeply the samples are sequenced.
    How to read: a tumour is normally sequenced deeper than its normal. A sample far below the rest may be too shallow to call variants; BamTools documents no floor.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hartwigmedical/hmftools/master/bam-tools/README.md
  column: mean_coverage
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: mean coverage, quartiles over samples
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: total_reads_spread
  title: Total reads
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median count of reads per sample and the box shows the spread. It answers how much sequencing each sample received.
    How to read: read counts follow the depth, so an outlier here usually explains an outlier in mean coverage.
  column: total_reads
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: reads, quartiles over samples

- component: card
  id: worst_duplicate_frac
  title: Highest duplicate fraction
  description: |-
    The hero number is the largest fraction of duplicate reads among the samples and the box shows the spread. It answers whether any library is dominated by duplicates.
    How to read: a high maximum next to low others marks one library with low complexity. Duplicates add depth without adding information.
  column: duplicate_frac
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: duplicate fraction, quartiles over samples

- component: card
  id: min_frac_ge_30x
  title: Lowest breadth at 30x
  description: |-
    The hero number is the smallest fraction of bases covered at 30x or more among the samples and the box shows the spread. It answers whether every sample reaches a useful depth over most of the genome.
    How to read: a low minimum marks the sample to check first. The 30x depth is one of the depths BamTools reports, not a pass mark.
  column: frac_ge_30x
  aggregation: min
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: fraction at 30x, quartiles over samples
  headline: true

- component: advanced_viz
  id: coverage_record
  title: Sample record
  description: |-
    One sample at a time: its reads, duplicates, coverage statistics and the fraction of bases lost to each quality filter. Select a row in the table to open it.
    How to read: compare the fractions lost to low mapping or base quality with the other samples to spot a failing library.
  kind: record_card
  roles:
    id: sample

- component: table
  id: bam_summary_table
  title: Alignment summary table
  description: |-
    Each row is a DNA sample with its read counts, coverage statistics, quality-loss fractions and the fraction of bases covered at each depth. It answers the exact figures behind the cards and lets a row selection filter the rest of the dashboard.
    How to read: sort by mean coverage or duplicate fraction to find the weakest sample.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: sample
